units.leftText: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

units.leftText: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.
units.rightText: it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

units.leftText: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.
units.rightText: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

units.leftText: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.” “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
units.rightText: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, The people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.

units.leftText: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
units.rightText: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?

units.leftText: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.
units.rightText: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul was leaning upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and the horsemen followed hard after him.

units.leftText: When he turned around and saw me, he called out to me, and I answered, ‘Here I am!’
units.rightText: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.

units.leftText: ‘Who are you?’ he asked. So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.

units.leftText: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Stand, I pray thee, beside me, and slay me; for anguish hath taken hold of me, because my life is yet whole in me.

units.leftText: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
units.rightText: So I stood beside him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.

units.leftText: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.
units.rightText: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:

units.leftText: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
units.rightText: and they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

units.leftText: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?” “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”
units.rightText: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.

units.leftText: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
units.rightText: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy Jehovah’s anointed?

units.leftText: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.
units.rightText: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him, so that he died.

units.leftText: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’” David’s Song for Saul and Jonathan
units.rightText: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain Jehovah’s anointed.

units.leftText: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,
units.rightText: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son

units.leftText: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
units.rightText: (and he bade them teach the children of Judah the song of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):
leftNotes: 1:18 Or be taught the use of the bow; literally be taught the bow
1:18 Or the Book of the Upright One, commonly cited as Jasher; note that the Song of the Bow that follows is not found in known manuscripts attributed to Jasher.

units.leftText: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
units.rightText: Thy glory, O Israel, is slain upon thy high places! How are the mighty fallen!

units.leftText: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
units.rightText: Tell it not in Gath, Publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon; Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

units.leftText: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
units.rightText: Ye mountains of Gilboa, Let there be no dew nor rain upon you, neither fields of offerings: For there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away, The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
leftNotes: 1:21 Or no showers falling on your terraced fields; LXX no fields of firstfruits; Hebrew no fields of offerings

units.leftText: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
units.rightText: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan turned not back, And the sword of Saul returned not empty.

units.leftText: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.
units.rightText: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they were not divided: They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions.

units.leftText: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.
units.rightText: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet delicately, Who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.

units.leftText: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
units.rightText: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain upon thy high places.

units.leftText: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
units.rightText: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: Very pleasant hast thou been unto me: Thy love to me was wonderful, Passing the love of women.

units.leftText: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”
units.rightText: How are the mighty fallen, And the weapons of war perished!

units.leftText: Some time later, David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?” “Go up,” the LORD answered. Then David asked, “Where should I go?” “To Hebron,” replied the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.

units.leftText: So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
units.rightText: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

units.leftText: David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.
units.rightText: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

units.leftText: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”
units.rightText: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, The men of Jabesh-gilead were they that buried Saul.

units.leftText: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.
units.rightText: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of Jehovah, that ye have showed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.

units.leftText: Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.
units.rightText: And now Jehovah show lovingkindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
leftNotes: 2:6 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.” Ish-bosheth Made King of Israel
units.rightText: Now therefore let your hands be strong, and be ye valiant; for Saul your lord is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim,
units.rightText: Now Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, had taken Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
leftNotes: 2:8 Ish-bosheth is also called Esh-baal; see 1 Chronicles 8:33|1CH 8:33*.

units.leftText: and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin— over all Israel.
units.rightText: and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

units.leftText: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years.
units.rightText: Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

units.leftText: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months. The Battle of Gibeon
units.rightText: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

units.leftText: One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
units.rightText: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

units.leftText: So Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two groups took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.
units.rightText: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.

units.leftText: Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.” “Let them get up,” Joab replied.
units.rightText: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men, I pray thee, arise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

units.leftText: So they got up and were counted off — twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.
units.rightText: Then they arose and went over by number: twelve for Benjamin, and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

units.leftText: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.
units.rightText: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
leftNotes: 2:16 Helkath-hazzurim means the Field of Swords.

units.leftText: The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.
units.rightText: And the battle was very sore that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.

units.leftText: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle,
units.rightText: And the three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.

units.leftText: and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.
units.rightText: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.

units.leftText: And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” “It is,” Asahel replied.
units.rightText: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Is it thou, Asahel? And he answered, It is I.

units.leftText: So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.” But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
units.rightText: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armor. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

units.leftText: Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”
units.rightText: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?

units.leftText: But Asahel refused to turn away. So Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.
units.rightText: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him in the body, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

units.leftText: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
units.rightText: But Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

units.leftText: The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.
units.rightText: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one band, and stood on the top of a hill.

units.leftText: Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”
units.rightText: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?

units.leftText: “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”
units.rightText: And Joab said, As God liveth, if thou hadst not spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone away, nor followed every one his brother.

units.leftText: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.
units.rightText: So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.

units.leftText: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.
units.rightText: And Abner and his men went all that night through the Arabah; and they passed over the Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
leftNotes: 2:29 See LXX; Hebrew marched all through Bithron

units.leftText: When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops.
units.rightText: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.

units.leftText: but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.
units.rightText: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, so that three hundred and threescore men died.

units.leftText: And they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.
units.rightText: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and the day brake upon them at Hebron.

units.leftText: Now the war between the house of Saul and the house of David was protracted. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.
units.rightText: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: and David waxed stronger and stronger, but the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.

units.leftText: And sons were born to David in Hebron: His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;
units.rightText: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his first-born was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

units.leftText: his second was Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; his third was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;
units.rightText: and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
leftNotes: 3:3 LXX Daluia; some translators Daniel; see 1 Chronicles 3:1|1CH 3:1*.

units.leftText: his fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; his fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital;
units.rightText: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

units.leftText: and his sixth was Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron. Abner Joins David
units.rightText: and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

units.leftText: During the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner had continued to strengthen his position in the house of Saul.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong in the house of Saul.

units.leftText: Now Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. So Ish-bosheth questioned Abner, “Why did you sleep with my father’s concubine?”
units.rightText: Now Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?

units.leftText: Abner was furious over Ish-bosheth’s accusation. “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah?” he asked. “All this time I have been loyal to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not delivered you into the hand of David, but now you accuse me of wrongdoing with this woman!
units.rightText: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog’s head that belongeth to Judah? This day do I show kindness unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David; and yet thou chargest me this day with a fault concerning this woman.

units.leftText: May God punish Abner, and ever so severely, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him:
units.rightText: God do so to Abner, and more also, if, as Jehovah hath sworn to David, I do not even so to him;

units.leftText: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
units.rightText: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: And for fear of Abner, Ish-bosheth did not dare to say another word to him.
units.rightText: And he could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.

units.leftText: Then Abner sent messengers on his behalf to say to David, “To whom does the land belong? Make your covenant with me, and surely my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
units.rightText: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.

units.leftText: “Good,” replied David, “I will make a covenant with you. But there is one thing I require of you: Do not appear before me unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to see me.”
units.rightText: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee; but one thing I require of thee: that is, thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.

units.leftText: Then David sent messengers to say to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, “Give me back my wife, Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
units.rightText: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

units.leftText: So Ish-bosheth sent and took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish.
units.rightText: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Paltiel the son of Laish.
leftNotes: 3:15 Paltiel is a variant of Palti; see 1 Samuel 25:44|1SA 25:44*.

units.leftText: Her husband followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go back.” So he returned home.
units.rightText: And her husband went with her, weeping as he went, and followed her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return: and he returned.

units.leftText: Now Abner conferred with the elders of Israel and said, “In the past you sought David as your king.
units.rightText: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, In times past ye sought for David to be king over you:

units.leftText: Now take action, because the LORD has said to David, ‘Through My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and of all their enemies.’”
units.rightText: now then do it; for Jehovah hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.

units.leftText: Abner also spoke to the Benjamites. Then he went to Hebron to tell David all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
units.rightText: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the whole house of Benjamin.

units.leftText: When Abner and twenty of his men came to David at Hebron, David held a feast for them.
units.rightText: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.

units.leftText: Then Abner said to David, “Let me go at once, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all that your heart desires.” So David dismissed Abner, and he went in peace. Joab Murders Abner
units.rightText: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy soul desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.

units.leftText: Just then David’s soldiers and Joab returned from a raid, bringing with them a great plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron, because David had sent him on his way in peace.
units.rightText: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a foray, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.

units.leftText: When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was informed, “Abner son of Ner came to see the king, who sent him on his way in peace.”
units.rightText: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.

units.leftText: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!
units.rightText: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?

units.leftText: Surely you realize that Abner son of Ner came to deceive you and to track your movements and all that you are doing.”
units.rightText: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.

units.leftText: As soon as Joab had left David, he sent messengers after Abner, who brought him back from the well of Sirah. But David was unaware of it.
units.rightText: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.

units.leftText: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pulled him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately, and there Joab stabbed him in the stomach. So Abner died on account of the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.
units.rightText: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there in the body, so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

units.leftText: Afterward, David heard about this and said, “I and my kingdom are forever guiltless before the LORD concerning the blood of Abner son of Ner.
units.rightText: And afterward, when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before Jehovah for ever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner:

units.leftText: May it whirl over the head of Joab and over the entire house of his father, and may the house of Joab never be without one having a discharge or skin disease, or one who leans on a staff or falls by the sword or lacks food.”
units.rightText: let it fall upon the head of Joab, and upon all his father’s house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth by the sword, or that lacketh bread.

units.leftText: (Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.) David Mourns for Abner
units.rightText: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

units.leftText: Then David ordered Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David himself walked behind the funeral bier.
units.rightText: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David followed the bier.

units.leftText: When they buried Abner in Hebron, the king wept aloud at Abner’s tomb, and all the people wept.
units.rightText: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.

units.leftText: And the king sang this lament for Abner: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?
units.rightText: And the king lamented for Abner, and said, Should Abner die as a fool dieth?

units.leftText: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not fettered. As a man falls before the wicked, so also you fell.” And all the people wept over him even more.
units.rightText: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: As a man falleth before the children of iniquity, so didst thou fall. And all the people wept again over him.

units.leftText: Then all the people came and urged David to eat something while it was still day, but David took an oath, saying, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!”
units.rightText: And all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David sware, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or aught else, till the sun be down.

units.leftText: All the people took note and were pleased. In fact, everything the king did pleased them.
units.rightText: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them; as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.

units.leftText: So on that day all the troops and all Israel were convinced that the king had no part in the murder of Abner son of Ner.
units.rightText: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.

units.leftText: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not realize that a great prince has fallen today in Israel?
units.rightText: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?

units.leftText: And I am weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!”
units.rightText: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me: Jehovah reward the evil-doer according to his wickedness.

units.leftText: Now when Ish-bosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost courage, and all Israel was dismayed.
units.rightText: And when Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

units.leftText: Saul’s son had two men who were leaders of raiding parties. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of the tribe of Benjamin— Beeroth is considered part of Benjamin,
units.rightText: And Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin (for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin:

units.leftText: because the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as foreigners to this day.
units.rightText: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day).

units.leftText: And Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she was hurrying to escape, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
units.rightText: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.

units.leftText: Now Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out and arrived at the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while the king was taking his midday nap.
units.rightText: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, as he took his rest at noon.

units.leftText: They entered the interior of the house as if to get some wheat, and they stabbed him in the stomach. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah slipped away.
units.rightText: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him in the body: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

units.leftText: They had entered the house while Ish-bosheth was lying on his bed, and having stabbed and killed him, they beheaded him, took his head, and traveled all night by way of the Arabah.
units.rightText: Now when they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went by the way of the Arabah all night.

units.leftText: They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. Today the LORD has granted vengeance to my lord the king against Saul and his offspring.” The Execution of Rechab and Baanah
units.rightText: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, thine enemy, who sought thy life; and Jehovah hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.

units.leftText: But David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,
units.rightText: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As Jehovah liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

units.leftText: when someone told me, ‘Look, Saul is dead,’ and thought he was a bearer of good news, I seized him and put him to death at Ziklag. That was his reward for his news!
units.rightText: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings.

units.leftText: How much more, when wicked men kill a righteous man in his own house and on his own bed, shall I not now require his blood from your hands and remove you from the earth!”
units.rightText: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, shall I not now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

units.leftText: So David commanded his young men, and they killed Rechab and Baanah. They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies by the pool in Hebron, but they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner’s tomb in Hebron.
units.rightText: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.

units.leftText: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.
units.rightText: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.

units.leftText: Even in times past, while Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. And to you the LORD said, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them.’”
units.rightText: In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah said to thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over Israel.

units.leftText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, where King David made with them a covenant before the LORD. And they anointed him king over Israel.
units.rightText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Jehovah: and they anointed David king over Israel.

units.leftText: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
units.rightText: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

units.leftText: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah. David Conquers Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 11:4–9|1CH 11:4-9*)
units.rightText: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.

units.leftText: Now the king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites who inhabited the land. The Jebusites said to David: “You will never get in here. Even the blind and lame can repel you.” For they thought, “David cannot get in here.”
units.rightText: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither; thinking, David cannot come in hither.

units.leftText: Nevertheless , David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).
units.rightText: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.

units.leftText: On that day he said, “Whoever attacks the Jebusites must use the water shaft to reach the lame and blind who are despised by David. ” That is why it is said, “The blind and the lame will never enter the palace.”
units.rightText: And David said on that day, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, let him get up to the watercourse, and smite the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul. Wherefore they say, There are the blind and the lame; he cannot come into the house.
leftNotes: 5:8 Or who are enemies of David

units.leftText: So David took up residence in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built it up all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.
units.rightText: And David dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.
leftNotes: 5:9 Hebrew the Millo

units.leftText: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD God of Hosts was with him.
units.rightText: And David waxed greater and greater; for Jehovah, the God of hosts, was with him.

units.leftText: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David. David’s Family Grows (1 Chronicles 14:1–7|1CH 14:1-7*)
units.rightText: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.

units.leftText: And David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.
units.rightText: And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.

units.leftText: After he had arrived from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
units.rightText: And David took him more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron; and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.

units.leftText: These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
units.rightText: And these are the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
leftNotes: 5:14 Shammua is a variant of Shimea; see 1 Chronicles 3:5|1CH 3:5*.

units.leftText: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
units.rightText: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,

units.leftText: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. Two Victories over the Philistines (1 Chronicles 14:8–17|1CH 14:8-17*)
units.rightText: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all went in search of him; but David learned of this and went down to the stronghold.
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the stronghold.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?” “Go up,” replied the LORD, “for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
units.rightText: And David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Jehovah said unto David, Go up; for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into thy hand.

units.leftText: So David went to Baal-perazim, where he defeated the Philistines and said, “Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me.” So he called that place Baal-perazim.
units.rightText: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there; and he said, Jehovah hath broken mine enemies before me, like the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
leftNotes: 5:20 Baal-perazim means The Lord Bursts Out.

units.leftText: There the Philistines abandoned their idols, and David and his men carried them away.
units.rightText: And they left their images there; and David and his men took them away.

units.leftText: Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: So David inquired of the LORD, who answered, “Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.
units.rightText: And when David inquired of Jehovah, he said, Thou shalt not go up: make a circuit behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.
leftNotes: 5:23 Or aspen trees or poplar trees; also in verse 24

units.leftText: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly, because this will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, when thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself; for then is Jehovah gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.

units.leftText: So David did as the LORD had commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.
units.rightText: And David did so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gezer.
leftNotes: 5:25 LXX (see also 1 Chronicles 14:16|1CH 14:16*); Hebrew Geba

units.leftText: David again assembled the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all.
units.rightText: And David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

units.leftText: And he and all his troops set out for Baale of Judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name— the name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim that are on it.
units.rightText: And David arose, and went with all the people that were with him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, which is called by the Name, even the name of Jehovah of hosts that sitteth above the cherubim.
leftNotes: 6:2 That is, Kiriath-jearim; see 1 Chronicles 13:6|1CH 13:6*.
6:2 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate do not include the Name—

units.leftText: They set the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart,
units.rightText: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that was in the hill: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.

units.leftText: bringing with it the ark of God. And Ahio was walking in front of the ark. Uzzah Touches the Ark (1 Chronicles 13:8–14|1CH 13:8-14*)
units.rightText: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, which was in the hill, with the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
leftNotes: 6:4 DSS and some LXX manuscripts; MT includes from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill.

units.leftText: David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
units.rightText: And David and all the house of Israel played before Jehovah with all manner of instruments made of fir-wood, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with castanets, and with cymbals.
leftNotes: 6:5 Literally before the LORD with all woods of cypress; LXX playing before the Lord on well-tuned instruments mightily, and with songs; some of the instruments in this verse are uncertain; see 1 Chronicles 13:8|1CH 13:8*.

units.leftText: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled.
units.rightText: And when they came to the threshing-floor of Nacon, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen stumbled.
leftNotes: 6:6 Nacon is a variant of Chidon; see 1 Chronicles 13:9|1CH 13:9*.

units.leftText: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
leftNotes: 6:7 MT; DSS for this

units.leftText: Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.
units.rightText: And David was displeased, because Jehovah had broken forth upon Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, unto this day.
leftNotes: 6:8 Perez-uzzah means outbreak against Uzzah.

units.leftText: That day David feared the LORD and asked, “How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?”
units.rightText: And David was afraid of Jehovah that day; and he said, How shall the ark of Jehovah come unto me?

units.leftText: So he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
units.rightText: So David would not remove the ark of Jehovah unto him into the city of David; but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

units.leftText: Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household. The Ark Brought to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:1–28|1CH 15:1-28*)
units.rightText: And the ark of Jehovah remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and Jehovah blessed Obed-edom, and all his house.

units.leftText: Now it was reported to King David, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God.”
units.rightText: And it was told king David, saying, Jehovah hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with joy.

units.leftText: When those carrying the ark of the LORD had advanced six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when they that bare the ark of Jehovah had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.

units.leftText: And David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD,
units.rightText: And David danced before Jehovah with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.

units.leftText: while he and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sounding of the ram’s horn. Michal’s Contempt for David (1 Chronicles 15:29–16:3|1CH 15:29-16:3*)
units.rightText: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of Jehovah with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

units.leftText: As the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
units.rightText: And it was so, as the ark of Jehovah came into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Jehovah; and she despised him in her heart.

units.leftText: So they brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
units.rightText: And they brought in the ark of Jehovah, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Jehovah.

units.leftText: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: And when David had made an end of offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: Then he distributed to every man and woman among the multitude of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake. And all the people departed, each to his own home.
units.rightText: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to every one a cake of bread, and a portion of flesh, and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed every one to his house.
leftNotes: 6:19 Or a portion of meat

units.leftText: When David returned home to bless his own household, Saul’s daughter Michal came out to meet him. “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” she said. “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do.”
units.rightText: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to-day, who uncovered himself to-day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

units.leftText: But David said to Michal, “I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me over your father and all his house when He appointed me ruler over the LORD’s people Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD,
units.rightText: And David said unto Michal, It was before Jehovah, who chose me above thy father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Jehovah, over Israel: therefore will I play before Jehovah.

units.leftText: and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this. Yet I will be honored by the maidservants of whom you have spoken.”
units.rightText: And I will be yet more vile than this, and will be base in mine own sight: but of the handmaids of whom thou hast spoken, of them shall I be had in honor.

units.leftText: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.
units.rightText: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.

units.leftText: After the king had settled into his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the king dwelt in his house, and Jehovah had given him rest from all his enemies round about,

units.leftText: he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent.”
units.rightText: that the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.

units.leftText: And Nathan replied to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
units.rightText: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thy heart; for Jehovah is with thee.

units.leftText: But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
units.rightText: And it came to pass the same night, that the word of Jehovah came unto Nathan, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell My servant David that this is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?
units.rightText: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah, Shalt thou build me a house for me to dwell in?

units.leftText: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling.
units.rightText: for I have not dwelt in a house since the day that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

units.leftText: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people Israel, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
units.rightText: In all places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel, spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?
leftNotes: 7:7 Or tribes

units.leftText: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.
units.rightText: Now therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, that thou shouldest be prince over my people, over Israel;

units.leftText: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land.
units.rightText: and I have been with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee; and I will make thee a great name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth.

units.leftText: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning
units.rightText: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as at the first,

units.leftText: and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies.
units.rightText: and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; and I will cause thee to rest from all thine enemies. Moreover Jehovah telleth thee that Jehovah will make thee a house.

units.leftText: And when your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
units.rightText: When thy days are fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, that shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.

units.leftText: He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
units.rightText: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.

units.leftText: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
units.rightText: I will be his father, and he shall be my son: if he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
leftNotes: 7:14 Cited in Hebrews 1:5|HEB 1:5*

units.leftText: But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
units.rightText: but my lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee.

units.leftText: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.”
units.rightText: And thy house and thy kingdom shall be made sure for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
leftNotes: 7:16 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX; most Hebrew manuscripts you

units.leftText: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire revelation. David’s Prayer of Thanksgiving (1 Chronicles 17:16–27|1CH 17:16-27*)
units.rightText: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.

units.leftText: Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
units.rightText: Then David the king went in, and sat before Jehovah; and he said, Who am I, O Lord Jehovah, and what is my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?

units.leftText: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant. Is this Your custom with man, O Lord GOD?
units.rightText: And this was yet a small thing in thine eyes, O Lord Jehovah; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant’s house for a great while to come; and this too after the manner of men, O Lord Jehovah!
leftNotes: 7:19 Or And this is Your instruction for mankind, O Lord GOD.

units.leftText: What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.
units.rightText: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou knowest thy servant, O Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and revealed it to Your servant.
units.rightText: For thy word’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou wrought all this greatness, to make thy servant know it.

units.leftText: How great You are, O Lord GOD! For there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
units.rightText: Wherefore thou art great, O Jehovah God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

units.leftText: And who is like Your people Israel — the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself and to make a name for Himself? You performed great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt.
units.rightText: And what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem unto himself for a people, and to make him a name, and to do great things for you, and terrible things for thy land, before thy people, whom thou redeemedst to thee out of Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
leftNotes: 7:23 See LXX and 1 Chronicles 17:21|1CH 17:21*; Hebrew You performed for Yourself great and awesome wonders for Your land, before Your people, whom You have redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from nations and their gods.

units.leftText: For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
units.rightText: And thou didst establish to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever; and thou, Jehovah, becamest their God.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house. Do as You have promised,
units.rightText: And now, O Jehovah God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, confirm thou it for ever, and do as thou hast spoken.

units.leftText: so that Your name will be magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be established before You.
units.rightText: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, Jehovah of hosts is God over Israel; and the house of thy servant David shall be established before thee.

units.leftText: For You, O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant when You said, ‘I will build a house for you.’ Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You.
units.rightText: For thou, O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee a house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.

units.leftText: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
units.rightText: And now, O Lord Jehovah, thou art God, and thy words are truth, and thou hast promised this good thing unto thy servant:

units.leftText: Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever.”
units.rightText: now therefore let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee; for thou, O Lord Jehovah, hast spoken it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.

units.leftText: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.
leftNotes: 8:1 Metheg-ammah means bridle of the mother city.

units.leftText: David also defeated the Moabites, made them lie down on the ground, and measured them off with a cord. He measured off with two lengths those to be put to death, and with one length those to be spared. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.
units.rightText: And he smote Moab, and measured them with the line, making them to lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. And the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.

units.leftText: David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, who had marched out to restore his dominion along the Euphrates River.
units.rightText: David smote also Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his dominion at the River.
leftNotes: 8:3 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate (see also 1 Chronicles 18:3|1CH 18:3*); Hebrew along the River, or an alternate reading along the Euphrates

units.leftText: David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.
units.rightText: And David took from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David hocked all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.
leftNotes: 8:4 LXX (see also DSS and 1 Chronicles 18:4|1CH 18:4*); MT captured from him seventeen hundred charioteers

units.leftText: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of their men.
units.rightText: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadadezer king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

units.leftText: Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
units.rightText: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.

units.leftText: And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a large amount of bronze.
units.rightText: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
leftNotes: 8:8 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Tebah; see 1 Chronicles 18:8|1CH 18:8*.

units.leftText: When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer,
units.rightText: And when Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
leftNotes: 8:9 Toi is a variant of Tou; also in verse 10; see 1 Chronicles 18:9|1CH 18:9*.

units.leftText: he sent his son Joram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver and gold and bronze,
units.rightText: then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
leftNotes: 8:10 Joram is a variant of Hadoram; see 1 Chronicles 18:10|1CH 18:10*.

units.leftText: and King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued—
units.rightText: these also did king David dedicate unto Jehovah, with the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations which he subdued;

units.leftText: from Edom and Moab, from the Ammonites and Philistines and Amalekites, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
units.rightText: of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
leftNotes: 8:12 Some Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, and Syriac (see also verse 14 and 1 Chronicles 18:11|1CH 18:11*); most Hebrew manuscripts Aram

units.leftText: And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
units.rightText: And David gat him a name when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the Valley of Salt, even eighteen thousand men.
leftNotes: 8:13 A few Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, and Syriac (see also verse 14 and 1 Chronicles 18:12|1CH 18:12*); most Hebrew manuscripts Arameans

units.leftText: He placed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went. David’s Officers (1 Chronicles 18:14–17|1CH 18:14-17*)
units.rightText: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Jehovah gave victory to David whithersoever he went.

units.leftText: Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:
units.rightText: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness unto all his people.

units.leftText: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
units.rightText: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;

units.leftText: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was the scribe;
units.rightText: and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; and Seraiah was scribe;
leftNotes: 8:17 Seraiah is also called Sheva, Shisha, and Shavsha; see 2 Samuel 20:25|2SA 20:25*, 1 Kings 4:3, and 1 Chronicles 18:16.

units.leftText: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; and David’s sons were priestly leaders.
units.rightText: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief ministers.
leftNotes: 8:18 Literally priests, or possibly chief officials; see LXX, Targum Yonaton, and 1 Chronicles 18:17|1CH 18:17*.

units.leftText: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”
units.rightText: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?

units.leftText: And there was a servant of the house of Saul named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.
units.rightText: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him unto David; and the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.

units.leftText: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of the house of Saul to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”
units.rightText: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, who is lame of his feet.

units.leftText: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.

units.leftText: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
units.rightText: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

units.leftText: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.
units.rightText: And Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came unto David, and fell on his face, and did obeisance. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold, thy servant!
leftNotes: 9:6 Mephibosheth is also called Merib-baal; see 1 Chronicles 8:34|1CH 8:34*.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
units.rightText: And David said unto him, Fear not; for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

units.leftText: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”
units.rightText: And he did obeisance, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?

units.leftText: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
units.rightText: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, All that pertained to Saul and to all his house have I given unto thy master’s son.

units.leftText: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.”
units.rightText: And thou shalt till the land for him, thou, and thy sons, and thy servants; and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master’s son may have bread to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

units.leftText: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.”
units.rightText: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king commandeth his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.

units.leftText: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
units.rightText: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
leftNotes: 9:12 Mica is a variant of Micah; see 1 Chronicles 8:34|1CH 8:34*.

units.leftText: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.
units.rightText: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem; for he did eat continually at the king’s table. And he was lame in both his feet.

units.leftText: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.”
units.rightText: And David said, I will show kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness unto me. So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Has not David instead sent his servants to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
units.rightText: But the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, in that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David sent his servants unto thee to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

units.leftText: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
units.rightText: So Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

units.leftText: When this was reported to David, he sent messengers to meet the men, since they had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
units.rightText: When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them; for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.

units.leftText: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba, as well as a thousand men from the king of Maacah and twelve thousand men from Tob.
units.rightText: And when the children of Ammon saw that they were become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.

units.leftText: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
units.rightText: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

units.leftText: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance of the city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country. David Defeats Ammon and Aram (1 Chronicles 19:10–19|1CH 19:10-19*)
units.rightText: And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.

units.leftText: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
units.rightText: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:

units.leftText: And he placed the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.
units.rightText: and the rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.
units.rightText: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me; but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.

units.leftText: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
units.rightText: Be of good courage, and let us play the man for our people, and for the cities of our God: and Jehovah do that which seemeth him good.

units.leftText: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.
units.rightText: So Joab and the people that were with him drew nigh unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.

units.leftText: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they regrouped.
units.rightText: And when the Syrians saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they gathered themselves together.

units.leftText: Hadadezer sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, and they came to Helam with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
units.rightText: And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the River: and they came to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.
leftNotes: 10:16 Hebrew the River
10:16 Shobach is a variant of Shophach; see 1 Chronicles 19:16|1CH 19:16*.
