units.leftText: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and went to Helam. Then the Arameans arrayed themselves against David and fought against him.
units.rightText: And it was told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.

units.leftText: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.
units.rightText: And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew of the Syrians the men of seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, so that he died there.
leftNotes: 10:18 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 19:18|1CH 19:18*); Hebrew horsemen

units.leftText: When all the kings who were subject to Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.
units.rightText: And when all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.

units.leftText: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, at the return of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 11:1 Literally At the turn of the year

units.leftText: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing— a very beautiful woman.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at eventide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.

units.leftText: So David sent and inquired about the woman, and he was told, “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
units.rightText: And David sent and inquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
leftNotes: 11:3 Eliam is a variant of Ammiel; see 1 Chronicles 3:5|1CH 3:5*.

units.leftText: Then David sent messengers to get her, and when she came to him, he slept with her. (Now she had just purified herself from her uncleanness.) Then she returned home.
units.rightText: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned unto her house.

units.leftText: And the woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”
units.rightText: And the woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, I am with child.

units.leftText: At this, David sent orders to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent him to David.
units.rightText: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.

units.leftText: When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab and the troops were doing and how the war was going.
units.rightText: And when Uriah was come unto him, David asked of him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.

units.leftText: Then he said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.”
units.rightText: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess of food from the king.

units.leftText: But Uriah slept at the door of the palace with all his master’s servants; he did not go down to his house.
units.rightText: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.

units.leftText: And David was told, “Uriah did not go home.” “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey?” David asked Uriah. “Why didn’t you go home?”
units.rightText: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Art thou not come from a journey? wherefore didst thou not go down unto thy house?

units.leftText: Uriah answered, “The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and my master Joab and his soldiers are camped in the open field. How can I go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!”
units.rightText: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in booths; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open field; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
leftNotes: 11:11 Or staying at Sukkoth

units.leftText: “Stay here one more day,” David said to Uriah, “and tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
units.rightText: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to-day also, and to-morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.

units.leftText: Then David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, and he got Uriah drunk. And in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his cot with his master’s servants, but he did not go home. David Arranges Uriah’s Death
units.rightText: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.

units.leftText: The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

units.leftText: In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”
units.rightText: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.

units.leftText: So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew the strongest enemy soldiers were.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Joab kept watch upon the city, that he assigned Uriah unto the place where he knew that valiant men were.

units.leftText: And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
units.rightText: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people, even of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

units.leftText: Joab sent to David a full account of the battle
units.rightText: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

units.leftText: and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished giving the king a full account of the battle,
units.rightText: and he charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling all the things concerning the war unto the king,

units.leftText: if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?
units.rightText: it shall be that, if the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore went ye so nigh unto the city to fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?

units.leftText: Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth ? Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’ If he asks you this, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’”
units.rightText: who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast an upper millstone upon him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? why went ye so nigh the wall? then shalt thou say, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
leftNotes: 11:21 Jerubbesheth is also known as Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon.

units.leftText: So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.
units.rightText: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.

units.leftText: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
units.rightText: And the messenger said unto David, The men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entrance of the gate.

units.leftText: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”
units.rightText: And the shooters shot at thy servants from off the wall; and some of the king’s servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

units.leftText: Then David told the messenger, “Say this to Joab: ‘Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.’ Encourage him with these words.” David Marries Bathsheba
units.rightText: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another; make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.

units.leftText: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
units.rightText: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she made lamentation for her husband.

units.leftText: And when the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
units.rightText: And when the mourning was past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David, and when he arrived, he said, “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.

units.leftText: The rich man had a great number of sheep and cattle,
units.rightText: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds;

units.leftText: but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food and drank from his cup; it slept in his arms and was like a daughter to him.
units.rightText: but the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own morsel, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
leftNotes: 12:3 Hebrew in his bosom; also in verse 8

units.leftText: Now a traveler came to the rich man, who refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for his guest.”
units.rightText: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him, but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.

units.leftText: David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan: “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
units.rightText: And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As Jehovah liveth, the man that hath done this is worthy to die:

units.leftText: Because he has done this thing and has shown no pity, he must pay for the lamb four times over.”
units.rightText: and he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

units.leftText: Then Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
units.rightText: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

units.leftText: I gave your master’s house to you and your master’s wives into your arms. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah, and if that was not enough, I would have given you even more.
units.rightText: and I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would have added unto thee such and such things.

units.leftText: Why then have you despised the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight? You put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as your own. You have slain him with the sword of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: Wherefore hast thou despised the word of Jehovah, to do that which is evil in his sight? thou hast smitten Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’
units.rightText: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thy house, because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: ‘I will raise up adversity against you from your own house. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to another, and he will lie with them in broad daylight.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house; and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbor, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.

units.leftText: You have acted in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’” David’s Loss and Repentance
units.rightText: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.

units.leftText: Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.”
units.rightText: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against Jehovah. And Nathan said unto David, Jehovah also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die.”
units.rightText: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of Jehovah to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
leftNotes: 12:14 DSS; MT you have brought utter contempt from the enemies of the LORD

units.leftText: After Nathan had gone home, the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.
units.rightText: And Nathan departed unto his house. And Jehovah struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.

units.leftText: David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.
units.rightText: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
leftNotes: 12:16 DSS and LXX; MT does not include in sackcloth.

units.leftText: The elders of his household stood beside him to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat anything with them.
units.rightText: And the elders of his house arose, and stood beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

units.leftText: On the seventh day the child died. But David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to us. So how can we tell him the child is dead? He may even harm himself.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he hearkened not unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead!

units.leftText: When David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, he perceived that the child was dead. So he asked his servants, “Is the child dead?” “He is dead,” they replied.
units.rightText: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

units.leftText: Then David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.
units.rightText: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel; and he came into the house of Jehovah, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.

units.leftText: “What is this you have done?” his servants asked. “While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when he died, you got up and ate.”
units.rightText: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.

units.leftText: David answered, “While the child was alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let him live.’
units.rightText: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who knoweth whether Jehovah will not be gracious to me, that the child may live?

units.leftText: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.” Solomon’s Birth
units.rightText: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me.

units.leftText: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon.
units.rightText: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon. And Jehovah loved him;
leftNotes: 12:24 Or she or he

units.leftText: and sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah because the LORD loved him. The Capture of Rabbah (1 Chronicles 20:1–3|1CH 20:1-3*)
units.rightText: and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, for Jehovah’s sake.
leftNotes: 12:25 Literally to name him Jedidiah because of the LORD; Jedidiah means beloved of the LORD

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.
units.rightText: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

units.leftText: Then Joab sent messengers to David to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.
units.rightText: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah; yea, I have taken the city of waters.
leftNotes: 12:27 Or and have captured the city of waters

units.leftText: Now, therefore, assemble the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city, and capture it. Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.”
units.rightText: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.

units.leftText: So David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah; and he fought against it and captured it.
units.rightText: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.

units.leftText: Then he took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
units.rightText: And he took the crown of their king from off his head; and the weight thereof was a talent of gold, and in it were precious stones; and it was set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.
leftNotes: 12:30 Or from the head of Milcom. Milcom, also called Molech, was god of the Ammonites; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.
12:30 A talent is approximately 75.4 pounds or 34.2 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. He did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 12:31 Literally put them under saws
12:31 Literally and he made them pass through the brick kilns.

units.leftText: After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

units.leftText: Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.
units.rightText: And Amnon was so vexed that he fell sick because of his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything unto her.

units.leftText: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very shrewd man,
units.rightText: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother: and Jonadab was a very subtle man.
leftNotes: 13:3 Shimeah is a variant of Shammah, Shimea, and Shimei; see 1 Samuel 16:9|1SA 16:9*, 2 Samuel 21:21, and 1 Chronicles 2:13.

units.leftText: and he asked Amnon, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon replied, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Why, O son of the king, art thou thus lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

units.leftText: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’”
units.rightText: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and feign thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, Let my sister Tamar come, I pray thee, and give me bread to eat, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.

units.leftText: So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”
units.rightText: So Amnon lay down, and feigned himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, Let my sister Tamar come, I pray thee, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.

units.leftText: Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”
units.rightText: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him food.

units.leftText: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.
units.rightText: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was laid down. And she took dough, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.

units.leftText: Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.
units.rightText: And she took the pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.

units.leftText: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.”
units.rightText: And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from thy hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.

units.leftText: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”
units.rightText: And when she had brought them near unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come, lie with me, my sister.

units.leftText: “No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not violate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!
units.rightText: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.

units.leftText: Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
units.rightText: And I, whither shall I carry my shame? and as for thee, thou wilt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.

units.leftText: But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.
units.rightText: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her, and lay with her.

units.leftText: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”
units.rightText: Then Amnon hated her with exceeding great hatred; for the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.

units.leftText: “No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!”
units.rightText: And she said unto him, Not so, because this great wrong in putting me forth is worse than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.

units.leftText: Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”
units.rightText: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.

units.leftText: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.
units.rightText: And she had a garment of divers colors upon her; for with such robes were the king’s daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
leftNotes: 13:18 Or a robe with long sleeves; see also Genesis 37:3|GEN 37:3*.

units.leftText: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying aloud.
units.rightText: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and went her way, crying aloud as she went.

units.leftText: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.
units.rightText: And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but now hold thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; take not this thing to heart. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.

units.leftText: When King David heard all this, he was furious.
units.rightText: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.
leftNotes: 13:21 DSS and LXX include But he would not punish his son Amnon, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn.

units.leftText: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar. Absalom’s Revenge on Amnon
units.rightText: And Absalom spake unto Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.

units.leftText: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheep-shearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

units.leftText: And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”
units.rightText: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheep-shearers; let the king, I pray thee, and his servants go with thy servant.

units.leftText: “No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.
units.rightText: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.

units.leftText: “If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.” “Why should he go with you?” the king asked.
units.rightText: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?

units.leftText: But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.
units.rightText: But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.
leftNotes: 13:27 LXX and Vulgate include And Absalom prepared a feast fit for a king.

units.leftText: Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”
units.rightText: And Absalom commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now, when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine; and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon, then kill him; fear not; have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.

units.leftText: So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.
units.rightText: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.

units.leftText: While they were on the way, a report reached David: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that the tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.

units.leftText: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground. And all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
units.rightText: Then the king arose, and rent his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.

units.leftText: But Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, spoke up: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead. In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
units.rightText: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.

units.leftText: So now, my lord the king, do not take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead.” Absalom Flees to Geshur
units.rightText: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for Amnon only is dead.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill. And the watchman went and reported to the king, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
units.rightText: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill-side behind him.
leftNotes: 13:34 Or behind him
13:34 LXX; Hebrew does not include And the watchman....

units.leftText: So Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.”
units.rightText: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king’s sons are come: as thy servant said, so it is.

units.leftText: And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice, and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.

units.leftText: Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But David mourned for his son every day.
units.rightText: But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.

units.leftText: After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
units.rightText: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

units.leftText: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
units.rightText: And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.
leftNotes: 13:39 MT; DSS and LXX And the spirit of the king
13:39 Or ceased to go out after Absalom

units.leftText: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.
units.rightText: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.

units.leftText: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.
units.rightText: And Joab sent to Tekoa, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on mourning apparel, I pray thee, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that hath a long time mourned for the dead:

units.leftText: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.
units.rightText: and go in to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

units.leftText: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”
units.rightText: And when the woman of Tekoa spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.

units.leftText: “What troubles you?” the king asked her.
units.rightText: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, Of a truth I am a widow, and my husband is dead.

units.leftText: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.
units.rightText: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and killed him.

units.leftText: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”
units.rightText: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thy handmaid, and they say, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he slew, and so destroy the heir also. Thus will they quench my coal which is left, and will leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the face of the earth.

units.leftText: “Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thy house, and I will give charge concerning thee.

units.leftText: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
units.rightText: And the woman of Tekoa said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house; and the king and his throne be guiltless.

units.leftText: “If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”
units.rightText: And the king said, Whosoever saith aught unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

units.leftText: “Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
units.rightText: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember Jehovah thy God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As Jehovah liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.

units.leftText: Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?” “Speak,” he replied.
units.rightText: Then the woman said, Let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak a word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.

units.leftText: The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?
units.rightText: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou devised such a thing against the people of God? for in speaking this word the king is as one that is guilty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished one.

units.leftText: For we will surely die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life, but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.
units.rightText: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God take away life, but deviseth means, that he that is banished be not an outcast from him.

units.leftText: Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.
units.rightText: Now therefore seeing that I am come to speak this word unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.

units.leftText: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
units.rightText: For the king will hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

units.leftText: And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’”
units.rightText: Then thy handmaid said, Let, I pray thee, the word of my lord the king be comfortable; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: and Jehovah thy God be with thee.
leftNotes: 14:17 Or Angel; also in verse 20

units.leftText: Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!” “Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.
units.rightText: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, aught that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

units.leftText: So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?”
units.rightText: And the king said, Is the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from aught that my lord the king hath spoken; for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thy handmaid;

units.leftText: Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”
units.rightText: to change the face of the matter hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.

units.leftText: Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom back.

units.leftText: Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”
units.rightText: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and did obeisance, and blessed the king; and Joab said, To-day thy servant knoweth that I have found favor in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath performed the request of his servant.

units.leftText: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the face of the king.
units.rightText: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, but let him not see my face. So Absalom turned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.

units.leftText: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.
units.rightText: Now in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

units.leftText: And when he cut the hair of his head— he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy— he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.
units.rightText: And when he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year’s end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, therefore he cut it); he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king’s weight.
leftNotes: 14:26 200 shekels is approximately 5 pounds or 2.3 kilograms of hair.

units.leftText: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman. Absalom Reconciled to David
units.rightText: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.

units.leftText: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.
units.rightText: And Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem; and he saw not the king’s face.

units.leftText: Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.
units.rightText: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king; but he would not come to him: and he sent again a second time, but he would not come.

units.leftText: Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!” And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
units.rightText: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
leftNotes: 14:30 LXX includes So the servants of Joab came to him with their clothes torn and said to him, “The servants of Absalom have set your field on fire.”

units.leftText: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
units.rightText: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?

units.leftText: “Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”
units.rightText: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it were better for me to be there still. Now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be iniquity in me, let him kill me.

units.leftText: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.
units.rightText: So Joab came to the king, and told him; and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

units.leftText: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

units.leftText: He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate.
units.rightText: And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that, when any man had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”
units.rightText: And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.

units.leftText: And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”
units.rightText: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!

units.leftText: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when any man came nigh to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him.

units.leftText: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
units.rightText: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

units.leftText: After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto Jehovah, in Hebron.
leftNotes: 15:7 Syriac and some LXX manuscripts; Hebrew forty

units.leftText: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’ ”
units.rightText: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If Jehovah shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I will serve Jehovah.
leftNotes: 15:8 Some LXX manuscripts; Hebrew does not include in Hebron.

units.leftText: “Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.
units.rightText: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.

units.leftText: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’”
units.rightText: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom is king in Hebron.

units.leftText: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.
units.rightText: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were invited, and went in their simplicity; and they knew not anything.

units.leftText: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing. David Flees Jerusalem (Psalm 3:1–8|PSA 3:1-8*)
units.rightText: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.

units.leftText: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
units.rightText: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

units.leftText: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”
units.rightText: And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for else none of us shall escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us quickly, and bring down evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.

units.leftText: The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”
units.rightText: And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall choose.

units.leftText: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.
units.rightText: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, that were concubines, to keep the house.

units.leftText: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,
units.rightText: And the king went forth, and all the people after him; and they tarried in Beth-merhak.

units.leftText: and all his servants marched past him — all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
units.rightText: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men that came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

units.leftText: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.
units.rightText: Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return, and abide with the king: for thou art a foreigner, and also an exile; return to thine own place.

units.leftText: In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness. ”
units.rightText: Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us, seeing I go whither I may? return thou, and take back thy brethren; mercy and truth be with thee.
leftNotes: 15:20 LXX; Hebrew May loving devotion and faithfulness be with you.

units.leftText: But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”
units.rightText: And Ittai answered the king, and said, As Jehovah liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether for death or for life, even there also will thy servant be.

units.leftText: “March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
units.rightText: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.

units.leftText: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
units.rightText: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.

units.leftText: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had passed out of the city.
units.rightText: And, lo, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
leftNotes: 15:24 Or Abiathar went up

units.leftText: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
units.rightText: And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favor in the eyes of Jehovah, he will bring me again, and show me both it, and his habitation:

units.leftText: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
units.rightText: but if he say thus, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.

units.leftText: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace— you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
units.rightText: The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art thou not a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
leftNotes: 15:27 Hebrew; LXX Behold,
15:27 Literally your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons with you

units.leftText: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
units.rightText: See, I will tarry at the fords of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.

units.leftText: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there. David Weeps at the Mount of Olives (Psalm 63:1–11|PSA 63:1-11*)
units.rightText: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they abode there.

units.leftText: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
units.rightText: And David went up by the ascent of the mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered, and went barefoot: and all the people that were with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

units.leftText: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
units.rightText: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O Jehovah, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

units.leftText: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when David was come to the top of the ascent, where God was worshipped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head.

units.leftText: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
units.rightText: And David said unto him, If thou passest on with me, then thou wilt be a burden unto me:

units.leftText: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
units.rightText: but if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father’s servant in time past, so will I now be thy servant; then wilt thou defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

units.leftText: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
units.rightText: And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

units.leftText: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
units.rightText: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son; and by them ye shall send unto me everything that ye shall hear.

units.leftText: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
units.rightText: So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
units.rightText: And when David was a little past the top of the ascent, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and a hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

units.leftText: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as are faint in the wilderness may drink.

units.leftText: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
units.rightText: And the king said, And where is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem; for he said, To-day will the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.

units.leftText: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!” Shimei Curses David
units.rightText: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine is all that pertaineth unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I do obeisance; let me find favor in thy sight, my lord, O king.

units.leftText: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
units.rightText: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, there came out thence a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera; he came out, and cursed still as he came.

units.leftText: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
units.rightText: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

units.leftText: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
units.rightText: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Begone, begone, thou man of blood, and base fellow:

units.leftText: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
units.rightText: Jehovah hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and Jehovah hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son; and, behold, thou art taken in thine own mischief, because thou art a man of blood.

units.leftText: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
units.rightText: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

units.leftText: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
units.rightText: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Because he curseth, and because Jehovah hath said unto him, Curse David; who then shall say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

units.leftText: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
units.rightText: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, who came forth from my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more may this Benjamite now do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for Jehovah hath bidden him.

units.leftText: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
units.rightText: It may be that Jehovah will look on the wrong done unto me, and that Jehovah will requite me good for his cursing of me this day.

units.leftText: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
units.rightText: So David and his men went by the way; and Shimei went along on the hill-side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.

units.leftText: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself. The Counsel of Ahithophel and Hushai
units.rightText: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary; and he refreshed himself there.
leftNotes: 16:14 Some LXX manuscripts arrived at the Jordan

units.leftText: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
units.rightText: And Absalom, and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

units.leftText: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, Long live the king, Long live the king.

units.leftText: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
units.rightText: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?

units.leftText: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by this people, and by all the men of Israel — his I will be, and with him I will remain.
units.rightText: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom Jehovah, and this people, and all the men of Israel have chosen, his will I be, and with him will I abide.

units.leftText: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not his son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
units.rightText: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.

units.leftText: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
units.rightText: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give your counsel what we shall do.

units.leftText: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to take care of the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
units.rightText: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, that he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel will hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then will the hands of all that are with thee be strong.

units.leftText: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
units.rightText: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

units.leftText: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
units.rightText: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those days, was as if a man inquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

units.leftText: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
units.rightText: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:

units.leftText: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king
units.rightText: and I will come upon him while he is weary and weak-handed, and will make him afraid; and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only;

units.leftText: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
units.rightText: and I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
leftNotes: 17:3 LXX; see also DSS; MT and bring all the people back to you. When everyone returns except the man you seek,

units.leftText: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
units.rightText: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.

units.leftText: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
units.rightText: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.

units.leftText: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
units.rightText: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not, speak thou.

units.leftText: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
units.rightText: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given this time is not good.

units.leftText: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
units.rightText: Hushai said moreover, Thou knowest thy father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field; and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

units.leftText: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
units.rightText: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them are fallen at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
leftNotes: 17:9 Or If he should attack your troops first

units.leftText: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
units.rightText: And even he that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they that are with him are valiant men.

units.leftText: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba— a multitude like the sand on the seashore— be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
units.rightText: But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together unto thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.

units.leftText: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
units.rightText: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground; and of him and of all the men that are with him we will not leave so much as one.

units.leftText: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found there.”
units.rightText: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.

units.leftText: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom. Hushai’s Warning Saves David (Psalm 55:1–23|PSA 55:1-23*)
units.rightText: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For Jehovah had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Jehovah might bring evil upon Absalom.

units.leftText: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
units.rightText: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.

units.leftText: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”
units.rightText: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.

units.leftText: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
units.rightText: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by En-rogel; and a maid-servant used to go and tell them; and they went and told king David: for they might not be seen to come into the city.

units.leftText: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
units.rightText: But a lad saw them, and told Absalom: and they went both of them away quickly, and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his court; and they went down thither.

units.leftText: Then the man’s wife took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
units.rightText: And the woman took and spread the covering over the well’s mouth, and strewed bruised grain thereon; and nothing was known.

units.leftText: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house; and they said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They are gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David; and they said unto David, Arise ye, and pass quickly over the water; for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.

units.leftText: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
units.rightText: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over the Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over the Jordan.

units.leftText: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
units.rightText: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home, unto his city, and set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.

units.leftText: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
units.rightText: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

units.leftText: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
units.rightText: And Absalom set Amasa over the host instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man, whose name was Ithra the Israelite, that went in to Abigal the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
leftNotes: 17:25 Ithra is a variant of Jether; see 1 Kings 2:5|1KI 2:5*.
17:25 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 2:17|1CH 2:17*); MT and other LXX manuscripts Israelite
17:25 Or Abigal, a variant of Abigail
17:25 Or of Jesse; see DSS and 1 Chronicles 2:13–16|1CH 2:13-16*

units.leftText: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
units.rightText: And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.

units.leftText: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,

units.leftText: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
units.rightText: brought beds, and basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and meal, and parched grain, and beans, and lentils, and parched pulse,
leftNotes: 17:28 Most LXX manuscripts and Syriac; Hebrew includes roasted seeds.

units.leftText: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
units.rightText: and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people are hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
units.rightText: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

units.leftText: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
units.rightText: And David sent forth the people, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
