units.leftText: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will not care about us. Even if half of us die, they will not care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better now if you support us from the city.”
units.rightText: But the people said, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but thou art worth ten thousand of us; therefore now it is better that thou be ready to succor us out of the city.
leftNotes: 18:3 Two Hebrew manuscripts, some LXX manuscripts, and Vulgate; most Hebrew manuscripts care; for now there are ten thousand like us

units.leftText: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
units.rightText: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate-side, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

units.leftText: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
units.rightText: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

units.leftText: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
units.rightText: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

units.leftText: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day— twenty thousand men.
units.rightText: And the people of Israel were smitten there before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter there that day of twenty thousand men.

units.leftText: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
units.rightText: For the battle was there spread over the face of all the country; and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

units.leftText: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
units.rightText: And Absalom chanced to meet the servants of David. And Absalom was riding upon his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between heaven and earth; and the mule that was under him went on.
leftNotes: 18:9 Or large terebinth or very great tree; similarly in verses 10 and 14

units.leftText: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
units.rightText: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak.

units.leftText: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
units.rightText: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest it, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten pieces of silver, and a girdle.
leftNotes: 18:11 10 shekels is approximately 4 ounces or 114 grams of silver.

units.leftText: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake. ’
units.rightText: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, yet would I not put forth my hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
leftNotes: 18:12 1,000 shekels is approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver.
18:12 A few Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts Whoever you may be, protect the young man Absalom. or Let no one touch the young man Absalom.

units.leftText: If I had jeopardized my own life — and nothing is hidden from the king— you would have abandoned me.”
units.rightText: Otherwise if I had dealt falsely against his life (and there is no matter hid from the king), then thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
leftNotes: 18:13 Or If I had dealt treacherously against his life

units.leftText: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
units.rightText: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

units.leftText: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
units.rightText: And ten young men that bare Joab’s armor compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.

units.leftText: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
units.rightText: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held back the people.

units.leftText: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
units.rightText: And they took Absalom, and cast him into the great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

units.leftText: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument. David Mourns for Absalom
units.rightText: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar, which is in the king’s dale; for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name; and it is called Absalom’s monument, unto this day.

units.leftText: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
units.rightText: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that Jehovah hath avenged him of his enemies.

units.leftText: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
units.rightText: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not be the bearer of tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day; but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.

units.leftText: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
units.rightText: Then said Joab to the Cushite, Go, tell the king what thou hast seen. And the Cushite bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.

units.leftText: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “No matter what, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
units.rightText: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But come what may, let me, I pray thee, also run after the Cushite. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou wilt have no reward for the tidings?

units.leftText: “No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
units.rightText: But come what may, said he, I will run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.
leftNotes: 18:23 That is, the plain of the Jordan

units.leftText: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
units.rightText: Now David was sitting between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.

units.leftText: So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.”
units.rightText: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.

units.leftText: the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.
units.rightText: And the watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold, another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.

units.leftText: The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
units.rightText: And the watchman said, I think the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.

units.leftText: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
units.rightText: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he bowed himself before the king with his face to the earth, and said, Blessed be Jehovah thy God, who hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.

units.leftText: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
units.rightText: And the king said, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, even me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.

units.leftText: “Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.
units.rightText: And the king said, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.

units.leftText: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
units.rightText: And, behold, the Cushite came; and the Cushite said, Tidings for my lord the king; for Jehovah hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.

units.leftText: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto the Cushite, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And the Cushite answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise up against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.

units.leftText: The king was shaken and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
units.rightText: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

units.leftText: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
units.rightText: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.

units.leftText: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
units.rightText: And the victory that day was turned into mourning unto all the people; for the people heard say that day, The king grieveth for his son.

units.leftText: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
units.rightText: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people that are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

units.leftText: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
units.rightText: And the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

units.leftText: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
units.rightText: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, who this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;

units.leftText: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
units.rightText: in that thou lovest them that hate thee, and hatest them that love thee. For thou hast declared this day, that princes and servants are nought unto thee: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.

units.leftText: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!” David Restored as King
units.rightText: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants; for I swear by Jehovah, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry a man with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that hath befallen thee from thy youth until now.

units.leftText: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king.
units.rightText: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king is sitting in the gate: and all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his tent.

units.leftText: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
units.rightText: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land from Absalom.

units.leftText: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”
units.rightText: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?

units.leftText: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
units.rightText: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, to bring him to his house.

units.leftText: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’
units.rightText: Ye are my brethren, ye are my bone and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?

units.leftText: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from now on you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”
units.rightText: And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.

units.leftText: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
units.rightText: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent unto the king, saying, Return thou, and all thy servants.

units.leftText: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan. Shimei Pardoned
units.rightText: So the king returned, and came to the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.

units.leftText: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
units.rightText: And Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, who was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

units.leftText: along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants.
units.rightText: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went through the Jordan in the presence of the king.

units.leftText: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight.
units.rightText: And there went over a ferry-boat to bring over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, when he was come over the Jordan.

units.leftText: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.
units.rightText: And he said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.

units.leftText: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
units.rightText: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come this day the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.

units.leftText: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
units.rightText: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed Jehovah’s anointed?

units.leftText: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”
units.rightText: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?

units.leftText: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him. Mephibosheth Excused
units.rightText: And the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.

units.leftText: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.
units.rightText: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king; and he had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.

units.leftText: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?

units.leftText: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me,
units.rightText: And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go with the king; because thy servant is lame.
leftNotes: 19:26 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate Saddle a donkey for me; Hebrew I will saddle a donkey for myself

units.leftText: and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king.
units.rightText: And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore what is good in thine eyes.

units.leftText: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”
units.rightText: For all my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king; yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet that I should cry any more unto the king?

units.leftText: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I say, Thou and Ziba divide the land.

units.leftText: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!” David’s Kindness to Barzillai
units.rightText: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come in peace unto his own house.

units.leftText: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.
units.rightText: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim; and he went over the Jordan with the king, to conduct him over the Jordan.

units.leftText: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.
units.rightText: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king with sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man.

units.leftText: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will sustain thee with me in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
units.rightText: And Barzillai said unto the king, How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?

units.leftText: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
units.rightText: I am this day fourscore years old: can I discern between good and bad? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?

units.leftText: Your servant will go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
units.rightText: Thy servant would but just go over the Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?

units.leftText: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
units.rightText: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.

units.leftText: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
units.rightText: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.

units.leftText: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
units.rightText: And all the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over: and the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.

units.leftText: Then the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king. Contention over the King
units.rightText: So the king went over to Gilgal, and Chimham went over with him: and all the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

units.leftText: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
units.rightText: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and brought the king, and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?

units.leftText: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
units.rightText: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then are ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all at the king’s cost? or hath he given us any gift?

units.leftText: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah spoke more fiercely than the men of Israel.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

units.leftText: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
units.rightText: And there happened to be there a base fellow, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew the trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.

units.leftText: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So all the men of Israel went up from following David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
units.rightText: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and provided them with sustenance, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.

units.leftText: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
units.rightText: Then said the king to Amasa, Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and be thou here present.

units.leftText: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
units.rightText: So Amasa went to call the men of Judah together; but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.

units.leftText: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us. ”
units.rightText: And David said to Abishai, Now will Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.
leftNotes: 20:6 Or and snatch away our eyes or and do us serious harm

units.leftText: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
units.rightText: And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

units.leftText: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them.
units.rightText: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. And Joab was girded with his apparel of war that he had put on, and thereon was a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.

units.leftText: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
units.rightText: And Joab said to Amasa, Is it well with thee, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

units.leftText: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
units.rightText: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the body, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

units.leftText: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
units.rightText: And there stood by him one of Joab’s young men, and said, He that favoreth Joab, and he that is for David, let him follow Joab.

units.leftText: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
units.rightText: And Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a garment over him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.

units.leftText: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
units.rightText: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

units.leftText: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
units.rightText: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth-maacah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.
leftNotes: 20:14 Hebrew to Abel and Beth-maacah; see verse 15.
20:14 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate Bicrites

units.leftText: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city.
units.rightText: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, and they cast up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.

units.leftText: a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”
units.rightText: Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.

units.leftText: When he had come near to her, the woman asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he replied. “Listen to the words of your servant,” she said. “I am listening,” he answered.
units.rightText: And he came near unto her; and the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thy handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.

units.leftText: Then the woman said, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Seek counsel at Abel,’ and that is how disputes were settled.
units.rightText: Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.

units.leftText: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
units.rightText: I am of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of Jehovah?

units.leftText: “Far be it!” Joab declared. “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
units.rightText: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

units.leftText: That is not the case. But a man named Sheba son of Bichri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.” “Look,” the woman replied, “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
units.rightText: The matter is not so: but a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David; deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

units.leftText: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and threw it out to Joab. And he blew the trumpet, and they were dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

units.leftText: Now Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites;
units.rightText: Now Joab was over all the host of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;

units.leftText: Adoram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
units.rightText: and Adoram was over the men subject to taskwork; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder;
leftNotes: 20:24 Adoram is a variant of Adoniram and Hadoram; see 1 Kings 4:6|1KI 4:6* and 2 Chronicles 10:18.

units.leftText: Sheva was the scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
units.rightText: and Sheva was scribe; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
leftNotes: 20:25 Sheva is also called Seraiah, Shisha, and Shavsha; see 2 Samuel 8:17|2SA 8:17*, 1 Kings 4:3, and 1 Chronicles 18:16.

units.leftText: and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.
units.rightText: and also Ira the Jairite was chief minister unto David.
leftNotes: 20:26 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts and Syriac Ithrite; see 2 Samuel 23:38|2SA 23:38*.

units.leftText: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”
units.rightText: And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David sought the face of Jehovah. And Jehovah said, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Gibeonites.

units.leftText: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)
units.rightText: And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah);

units.leftText: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”
units.rightText: and David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of Jehovah?

units.leftText: The Gibeonites said to him, “We need no silver or gold from Saul or his house, nor should you put to death anyone in Israel for us.” “Whatever you ask, I will do for you,” he replied.
units.rightText: And the Gibeonites said unto him, It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Saul, or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.

units.leftText: And they answered the king, “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel,
units.rightText: And they said unto the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Israel,

units.leftText: let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” “I will give them to you,” said the king.
units.rightText: let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto Jehovah in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Jehovah. And the king said, I will give them.
leftNotes: 21:6 Or expose them or execute them; similarly in verse 9

units.leftText: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
units.rightText: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Jehovah’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

units.leftText: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, as well as the five sons whom Merab daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
units.rightText: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bare to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:
leftNotes: 21:8 Two Hebrew manuscripts, some LXX manuscripts, and Syriac (see also 1 Samuel 18:19|1SA 18:19*); most Hebrew and LXX manuscripts Michal

units.leftText: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
units.rightText: and he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the mountain before Jehovah, and they fell all seven together. And they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

units.leftText: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
units.rightText: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured upon them from heaven; and she suffered neither the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

units.leftText: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done,
units.rightText: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

units.leftText: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hung the bodies after they had struck down Saul at Gilboa.
units.rightText: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, in the day that the Philistines slew Saul in Gilboa;

units.leftText: So David had the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan brought from there, and they also gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.
units.rightText: and he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son: and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

units.leftText: And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land. Four Battles against the Philistines (1 Chronicles 20:4–8|1CH 20:4-8*)
units.rightText: And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.

units.leftText: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines. But David became exhausted.
units.rightText: And the Philistines had war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines. And David waxed faint;

units.leftText: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.
units.rightText: and Ishbi-benob, who was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.
leftNotes: 21:16 Or the giant; also in verses 18, 20, and 22
21:16 300 shekels is approximately 7.5 pounds or 3.4 kilograms.

units.leftText: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”
units.rightText: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succored him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.

units.leftText: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, a descendant of Rapha.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after this, that there was again war with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Saph, who was of the sons of the giant.
leftNotes: 21:18 Saph is a variant of Sippai; see 1 Chronicles 20:4|1CH 20:4*.

units.leftText: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
units.rightText: And there was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim the Beth-lehemite slew Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
leftNotes: 21:19 See 1 Chronicles 20:5|1CH 20:5*; Hebrew Jaare-oregim
21:19 See 1 Chronicles 20:5|1CH 20:5*; Hebrew does not include the brother of.

units.leftText: And there was also a battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot— twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,
units.rightText: And there was again war at Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.

units.leftText: and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.
units.rightText: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimei, David’s brother, slew him.
leftNotes: 21:21 Shimei is a variant of Shammah, Shimeah, and Shimea; see 1 Samuel 16:9|1SA 16:9*, 2 Samuel 13:3, and 1 Chronicles 2:13.

units.leftText: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
units.rightText: These four were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

units.leftText: And David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
units.rightText: And David spake unto Jehovah the words of this song in the day that Jehovah delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:

units.leftText: He said: “The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.
units.rightText: and he said, Jehovah is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;

units.leftText: My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation. My stronghold, my refuge, and my Savior, You save me from violence.
units.rightText: God, my rock, in him will I take refuge; My shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge; My saviour, thou savest me from violence.

units.leftText: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies.
units.rightText: I will call upon Jehovah, who is worthy to be praised: So shall I be saved from mine enemies.

units.leftText: For the waves of death engulfed me; the torrents of chaos overwhelmed me.
units.rightText: For the waves of death compassed me; The floods of ungodliness made me afraid:

units.leftText: The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
units.rightText: The cords of Sheol were round about me; The snares of death came upon me.

units.leftText: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried out to my God. And from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help reached His ears.
units.rightText: In my distress I called upon Jehovah; Yea, I called unto my God: And he heard my voice out of his temple, And my cry came into his ears.

units.leftText: Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled; they were shaken because He burned with anger.
units.rightText: Then the earth shook and trembled, The foundations of heaven quaked And were shaken, because he was wroth.
leftNotes: 22:8 Most Hebrew sources; Vulgate, Syriac, and two Hebrew manuscripts (see also Psalm 18:7|PSA 18:7*) mountains

units.leftText: Smoke rose from His nostrils, and consuming fire came from His mouth; glowing coals blazed forth.
units.rightText: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, And fire out of his mouth devoured: Coals were kindled by it.

units.leftText: He parted the heavens and came down with dark clouds beneath His feet.
units.rightText: He bowed the heavens also, and came down; And thick darkness was under his feet.

units.leftText: He mounted a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind.
units.rightText: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly; Yea, he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
leftNotes: 22:11 Many Hebrew manuscripts (see also Psalm 18:10|PSA 18:10*); most Hebrew manuscripts He was seen

units.leftText: He made darkness a canopy around Him, a gathering of water and thick clouds.
units.rightText: And he made darkness pavilions round about him, Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

units.leftText: From the brightness of His presence coals of fire blazed forth.
units.rightText: At the brightness before him Coals of fire were kindled.
leftNotes: 22:13 Or bolts of lightning

units.leftText: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.
units.rightText: Jehovah thundered from heaven, And the Most High uttered his voice.

units.leftText: He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
units.rightText: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; Lightning, and discomfited them.

units.leftText: The channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were exposed at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
units.rightText: Then the channels of the sea appeared, The foundations of the world were laid bare, By the rebuke of Jehovah, At the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

units.leftText: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of deep waters.
units.rightText: He sent from on high, he took me; He drew me out of many waters;

units.leftText: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from foes too mighty for me.
units.rightText: He delivered me from my strong enemy, From them that hated me; for they were too mighty for me.

units.leftText: They confronted me in my day of calamity, but the LORD was my support.
units.rightText: They came upon me in the day of my calamity; But Jehovah was my stay.

units.leftText: He brought me out into the open; He rescued me because He delighted in me.
units.rightText: He brought me forth also into a large place; He delivered me, because he delighted in me.

units.leftText: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
units.rightText: Jehovah rewarded me according to my righteousness; According to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.

units.leftText: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.
units.rightText: For I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And have not wickedly departed from my God.

units.leftText: For all His ordinances are before me; I have not disregarded His statutes.
units.rightText: For all his ordinances were before me; And as for his statutes, I did not depart from them.

units.leftText: And I have been blameless before Him and kept myself from iniquity.
units.rightText: I was also perfect toward him; And I kept myself from mine iniquity.

units.leftText: So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight.
units.rightText: Therefore hath Jehovah recompensed me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his eyesight.
leftNotes: 22:25 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate (see also Psalm 18:24|PSA 18:24*) according to the cleanness of my hands

units.leftText: To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless;
units.rightText: With the merciful thou wilt show thyself merciful; With the perfect man thou wilt show thyself perfect;

units.leftText: to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
units.rightText: With the pure thou wilt show thyself pure; And with the perverse thou wilt show thyself froward.

units.leftText: You save an afflicted people, but Your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down.
units.rightText: And the afflicted people thou wilt save; But thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.

units.leftText: For You, O LORD, are my lamp; the LORD lights up my darkness.
units.rightText: For thou art my lamp, O Jehovah; And Jehovah will lighten my darkness.

units.leftText: For in You I can charge an army; with my God I can scale a wall.
units.rightText: For by thee I run upon a troop; By my God do I leap over a wall.

units.leftText: As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
units.rightText: As for God, his way is perfect: The word of Jehovah is tried; He is a shield unto all them that take refuge in him.

units.leftText: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?
units.rightText: For who is God, save Jehovah? And who is a rock, save our God?

units.leftText: God is my strong fortress, and He makes my way clear.
units.rightText: God is my strong fortress; And he guideth the perfect in his way.

units.leftText: He makes my feet like those of a deer and stations me upon the heights.
units.rightText: He maketh his feet like hinds’ feet, And setteth me upon my high places.

units.leftText: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
units.rightText: He teacheth my hands to war, So that mine arms do bend a bow of brass.

units.leftText: You have given me Your shield of salvation, and Your gentleness exalts me.
units.rightText: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation; And thy gentleness hath made me great.
leftNotes: 22:36 Or and Your help exalts me or and You stoop down to make me great

units.leftText: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.
units.rightText: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; And my feet have not slipped.

units.leftText: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
units.rightText: I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; Neither did I turn again till they were consumed.

units.leftText: I devoured and crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.
units.rightText: And I have consumed them, and smitten them through, so that they cannot arise: Yea, they are fallen under my feet.

units.leftText: You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me.
units.rightText: For thou hast girded me with strength unto the battle; Thou hast subdued under me those that rose up against me.

units.leftText: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I destroyed those who hated me.
units.rightText: Thou hast also made mine enemies turn their backs unto me, That I might cut off them that hate me.

units.leftText: They looked, but there was no one to save them — to the LORD, but He did not answer.
units.rightText: They looked, but there was none to save; Even unto Jehovah, but he answered them not.

units.leftText: I ground them as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.
units.rightText: Then did I beat them small as the dust of the earth, I did crush them as the mire of the streets, and did spread them abroad.

units.leftText: You have delivered me from the strife of my people; You have preserved me as the head of nations; a people I had not known shall serve me.
units.rightText: Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people; Thou hast kept me to be the head of the nations: A people whom I have not known shall serve me.

units.leftText: Foreigners cower before me; when they hear me, they obey me.
units.rightText: The foreigners shall submit themselves unto me: As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me.

units.leftText: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their strongholds.
units.rightText: The foreigners shall fade away, And shall come trembling out of their close places.
leftNotes: 22:46 Some LXX manuscripts and Vulgate (see also Psalm 18:45|PSA 18:45*); MT and arm themselves

units.leftText: The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—
units.rightText: Jehovah liveth; And blessed be my rock; And exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,

units.leftText: the God who avenges me and brings down nations beneath me,
units.rightText: Even the God that executeth vengeance for me, And that bringeth down peoples under me,

units.leftText: who frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.
units.rightText: And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: Yea, thou liftest me up above them that rise up against me; Thou deliverest me from the violent man.

units.leftText: Therefore I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to Your name.
units.rightText: Therefore I will give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah, among the nations, And will sing praises unto thy name.
leftNotes: 22:50 Cited in Romans 15:9|ROM 15:9*

units.leftText: Great salvation He brings to His king. He shows loving devotion to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”
units.rightText: Great deliverance giveth he to his king, And showeth lovingkindness to his anointed, To David and to his seed, for evermore.

units.leftText: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
units.rightText: Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse saith, And the man who was raised on high saith, The anointed of the God of Jacob, And the sweet psalmist of Israel:
leftNotes: 23:1 Or the hero of the songs of Israel or the favorite of the Strong One of Israel

units.leftText: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.
units.rightText: The Spirit of Jehovah spake by me, And his word was upon my tongue.

units.leftText: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
units.rightText: The God of Israel said, The Rock of Israel spake to me: One that ruleth over men righteously, That ruleth in the fear of God,

units.leftText: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’
units.rightText: He shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, A morning without clouds, When the tender grass springeth out of the earth, Through clear shining after rain.

units.leftText: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?
units.rightText: Verily my house is not so with God; Yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, Ordered in all things, and sure: For it is all my salvation, and all my desire, Although he maketh it not to grow.

units.leftText: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.
units.rightText: But the ungodly shall be all of them as thorns to be thrust away, Because they cannot be taken with the hand;

units.leftText: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.” David’s Mighty Men (1 Chronicles 11:10–47|1CH 11:10-47*)
units.rightText: But the man that toucheth them Must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear: And they shall be utterly burned with fire in their place.

units.leftText: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
units.rightText: These are the names of the mighty men whom David had: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.
leftNotes: 23:8 Tahchemonite is probably a variant of Hachmonite; see 1 Chronicles 11:11|1CH 11:11*.
23:8 Or chief among the captains
23:8 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 11:11|1CH 11:11*); Hebrew He was called Adino the Eznite because of

units.leftText: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,
units.rightText: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodai the son of an Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away.
leftNotes: 23:9 Dodo is a variant of Dodai; see 1 Chronicles 27:4|1CH 27:4*.

units.leftText: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.
units.rightText: He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword; and Jehovah wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to take spoil.

units.leftText: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.
units.rightText: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee a Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a plot of ground full of lentils; and the people fled from the Philistines.

units.leftText: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.
units.rightText: But he stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and slew the Philistines; and Jehovah wrought a great victory.

units.leftText: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: And three of the thirty chief men went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam; and the troop of the Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.
units.rightText: And David was then in the stronghold; and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth-lehem.

units.leftText: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
units.rightText: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me water to drink of the well of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate!

units.leftText: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead , he poured it out to the LORD,
units.rightText: And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: saying, “Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
units.rightText: And he said, Be it far from me, O Jehovah, that I should do this: shall I drink the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.

units.leftText: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
units.rightText: And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them, and had a name among the three.
leftNotes: 23:18 Most Hebrew manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 11:20|1CH 11:20*); two Hebrew manuscripts and Syriac the Thirty

units.leftText: Was he not more honored than the Three? And he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.
units.rightText: Was he not most honorable of the three? therefore he was made their captain: howbeit he attained not unto the first three.
leftNotes: 23:19 Hebrew; Syriac the Thirty

units.leftText: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
units.rightText: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, he slew the two sons of Ariel of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow.
leftNotes: 23:20 Or Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of Ishhai
23:20 Or two sons of Ariel

units.leftText: He also struck down an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
units.rightText: And he slew an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.

units.leftText: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name along with the three mighty men.
units.rightText: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had a name among the three mighty men.

units.leftText: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
units.rightText: He was more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him over his guard.

units.leftText: Now these were members of the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
units.rightText: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth-lehem,
leftNotes: 23:24 Literally In the Thirty (were):

units.leftText: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
units.rightText: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

units.leftText: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
units.rightText: Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,

units.leftText: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
units.rightText: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
leftNotes: 23:27 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Sibbecai; see 2 Samuel 21:18|2SA 21:18* and 1 Chronicles 11:29.

units.leftText: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
units.rightText: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,

units.leftText: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites,
units.rightText: Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
leftNotes: 23:29 Some Hebrew manuscripts and Vulgate (see also 1 Chronicles 11:30|1CH 11:30*); most MT manuscripts Heleb
23:29 Ittai is a variant of Ithai; see 1 Chronicles 11:31|1CH 11:31*.

units.leftText: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,
units.rightText: Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash.
leftNotes: 23:30 Hiddai is a variant of Hurai; see 1 Chronicles 11:32|1CH 11:32*.
23:30 Or from the ravines

units.leftText: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
units.rightText: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,

units.leftText: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen,
units.rightText: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
leftNotes: 23:32 Jashen is a variant of Hashem; see 1 Chronicles 11:34|1CH 11:34*.

units.leftText: son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
units.rightText: Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,
leftNotes: 23:33 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 11:34|1CH 11:34*); Hebrew Jonathan, 33*Shammah
23:33 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Sachar; see 1 Chronicles 11:35|1CH 11:35*.

units.leftText: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
units.rightText: Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

units.leftText: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
units.rightText: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,

units.leftText: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
units.rightText: Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,

units.leftText: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
units.rightText: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armorbearers to Joab the son of Zeruiah,

units.leftText: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
units.rightText: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

units.leftText: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
units.rightText: Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.

units.leftText: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
units.rightText: And again the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.

units.leftText: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”
units.rightText: And the king said to Joab the captain of the host, who was with him, Go now to and fro through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the sum of the people.
leftNotes: 24:2 LXX to Joab and the army commanders with him

units.leftText: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
units.rightText: And Joab said unto the king, Now Jehovah thy God add unto the people, how many soever they may be, a hundredfold; and may the eyes of my lord the king see it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?

units.leftText: Nevertheless , the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to register the troops of Israel.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.

units.leftText: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.
units.rightText: And they passed over the Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and unto Jazer:

units.leftText: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
units.rightText: then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan, and round about to Sidon,
leftNotes: 24:6 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts to Gilead and to the land of the Hittites

units.leftText: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
units.rightText: and came to the stronghold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites; and they went out to the south of Judah, at Beer-sheba.
leftNotes: 24:7 Or to the south of Judah

units.leftText: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So when they had gone to and fro through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

units.leftText: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000. Judgment for David’s Sin (1 Chronicles 21:7–13|1CH 21:7-13*)
units.rightText: And Joab gave up the sum of the numbering of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

units.leftText: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
units.rightText: And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto Jehovah, I have sinned greatly in that which I have done: but now, O Jehovah, put away, I beseech thee, the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

units.leftText: When David got up in the morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:
units.rightText: And when David rose up in the morning, the word of Jehovah came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”
units.rightText: Go and speak unto David, Thus saith Jehovah, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

units.leftText: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
units.rightText: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thy foes while they pursue thee? or shall there be three days’ pestilence in thy land? now advise thee, and consider what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
leftNotes: 24:13 LXX (see also 1 Chronicles 21:12|1CH 21:12*); Hebrew seven

units.leftText: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.” A Plague on Israel (1 Chronicles 21:14–17|1CH 21:14-17*)
units.rightText: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of Jehovah; for his mercies are great; and let me not fall into the hand of man.

units.leftText: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
units.rightText: So Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed; and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.
leftNotes: 24:15 Literally and of the people from Dan to Beersheba, seventy thousand men died

units.leftText: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
units.rightText: And when the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, Jehovah repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough; now stay thy hand. And the angel of Jehovah was by the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
leftNotes: 24:16 Araunah is a variant of Ornan; see 1 Chronicles 21:15|1CH 21:15* and 2 Chronicles 3:1.

units.leftText: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.” David Builds an Altar (1 Chronicles 21:18–30|1CH 21:18-30*)
units.rightText: And David spake unto Jehovah when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done perversely; but these sheep, what have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.
leftNotes: 24:17 DSS and LXX; MT does not include the shepherd.

units.leftText: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
units.rightText: And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

units.leftText: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
units.rightText: And David went up according to the saying of Gad, as Jehovah commanded.

units.leftText: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.
units.rightText: And Araunah looked forth, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.

units.leftText: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
units.rightText: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing-floor of thee, to build an altar unto Jehovah, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

units.leftText: Araunah said to David, “May my lord the king take whatever seems good to him and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
units.rightText: And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what seemeth good unto him: behold, the oxen for the burnt-offering, and the threshing instruments and the yokes of the oxen for the wood:

units.leftText: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
units.rightText: all this, O king, doth Araunah give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, Jehovah thy God accept thee.

units.leftText: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will verily buy it of thee at a price; neither will I offer burnt-offerings unto Jehovah my God which cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

units.leftText: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.
units.rightText: And David built there an altar unto Jehovah, and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings. So Jehovah was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
